In the community of St George’s School everyone is considered as an individual and is valued equally. Everyone is made to feel welcome and has a voice.
Our school is a safe place to achieve, have fun and to develop skills towards individual, informed paths as we leave school and move forward in life towards adulthood. Our Careers and Preparation for Adulthood Curriculum
At St George’s School, careers education is not a standalone programme. It is embedded throughout our curriculum and underpins our commitment to preparing students for successful adult lives. Through our values of Perseverance, Respect, Aspiration and Independence, we support every young person to understand themselves, develop their skills and make informed choices about their future.
Developing Essential Work Skills
From Key Stage 3 onwards, all students develop the essential skills needed for learning, work and adult life through the Skills Builder Framework.
The eight essential skills are systematically taught, practised and assessed across the curriculum:
These skills are embedded across specialist curriculum areas, enabling students to develop and apply them in meaningful and relevant contexts. Skills Builder assessments help students recognise their strengths, identify next steps and celebrate progress as they prepare for adulthood.
By embedding Skills Builder throughout Key Stage 3 and beyond, students develop the confidence, resilience and employability skills that employers consistently identify as essential for future success.
Our Three Preparation for Adulthood Pathways
Recognising that every young person has different strengths, aspirations and support needs, students access one of three personalised pathways.
The Vocational Pathway supports students who are working towards accredited qualifications and future employment opportunities.
Sixth Form Vocational Options
In Sixth Form, vocational options are carefully selected to reflect students’ individual aspirations, interests and intended destinations.

Whether a student progresses to college, employment, a supported internship, volunteering or community provision, our aim is that every learner leaves St George’s with the skills, confidence and aspiration to take their next steps successfully.

Information Education and Guidance at St George’s
At St George’s we believe in delivering a careers education that is engaging, sparks curiosity and is meaningful to our students, their needs and their lives. Where appropriate, we have committed to following the guidance outlined in the government’s Careers Strategy.
The careers leader at St George’s is responsible for making sure that the programme meets the expectations set out in the Gatsby Benchmarks.
We have a strong and stable careers programme, which is led by the interests and aspirations of students in regards to developing life skills, gaining independence, making choices, future learning and gaining employment, with a strong emphasis on vocational learning.
We are proud to be a Skills Builders school, which incorporates the eight essential skills needed for life through both our curriculum and wider opportunities. These are teamwork, speaking/communication, listening, leadership, aiming high, creativity, problem solving and staying positive.

Governance
Governing Bodies’ Core Functions
The department has high expectations of governing bodies. They are the strategic leaders of our schools and have a vital role to play in making sure every child gets the best possible education. For maintained schools this is reflected in the law, which states that the purpose of maintained school governing bodies is to ‘conduct the school with a view to promoting high standards of educational achievement at the school’
In all types of schools, governing bodies should have a strong focus on three core strategic functions:
This amounts to a demanding role for governing bodies. Evidence suggests that those that deliver it well do so by:
understanding their strategic role – building a productive and supportive relationship with the headteacher while holding them to account for school performance and taking hard strategic decisions in the light of objective data;
ensuring governors have the necessary skills and commitment, including to challenge the school to bring about improvement and hold leaders to account for performance;
appointing an effective chair to lead and manage the governing body.
appointing a high quality clerk to advise them on the nature of their functions and duties and ensure the governing body operates efficiently and effectively;
evaluating their performance regularly in the light of Ofsted expectations and other good practice and making changes as necessary to improve their effectiveness;
Effective governing bodies also think carefully about how they are organised. This includes thinking about whether and how to use their powers to delegate functions and decisions to committees or individual governors. Governing bodies may decide to task individual governors to take an interest in a specific area, such as SEN, safeguarding or health and safety, but there is no legal requirement for either maintained schools or academies to do so. There are many different models and governing bodies are best placed to decide for themselves what will work best in their own circumstances. It is the overall governing body, however, that in all cases remains accountable in law, to Ofsted and to the local community for the exercise of its functions. The department expects every governing body to focus strongly on its core functions and to retain oversight of them.
Steff Gleeson – Headteacher
I am Steff and have worked at St George’s for 12.5 years. In September 2022 I took on the role of Headteacher, this was never an ambition of mine, however when Sue Holman announced her retirement after 16 years I felt very strongly that I wanted to continue the improvement journey for St George’s. So after 12 years as the Deputy Head I decided to apply for the role of Headteacher.
It has been so much more than I expected and I am genuinely enjoying every moment, the challenges, the new elements to my role, working with such a dedicated team of staff, and most importantly the wonderful students.
My experience as a Governor previously has been as a member of the Island Learning Centre Management Committee. During my time at St George’s I have always attended and contributed to the Governing Body but this is the first time I have actually been a member of the Governing Body. I meet with Dave the Chair of Governors weekly and communication and interaction between the governors and school staff is good. There is also a high governor presence at all school events which is very positive.
As most of you know Poppy the school dog is mine, I am very proud of the fact that I trained her as a Pets as Therapy dog when she was young. She has been coming to St George’s since she was 8 weeks old, she is nearly 8 years old. Unfortunately she has arthritis and is quite stiff and getting slower (and more stubborn) but she still enjoys her role at school and loves spending time with the students.
When I am not at school I enjoy spending precious time with my family and looking after my animals. I have horses and they take up a lot of my spare time but also provide me with an enjoyable hobby.
Steve Hollinghurst – Chair of Governors
My role is to lead St George’s School Governors to both support and challenge the school in all aspects of its work to get the best outcomes for young people.
I have worked in special education for over 40 years. I retired in 2019 as an executive head of two special schools. I then did teacher supply work for 2 years. I also did some consultancy. I am now fully retired but enjoy the voluntary position of supporting a special school. I believe that all children deserve the best provision and I aim to help the staff at St. George’s to do this. I have many years’ experience as aschool governor. I was head of a special school for 8 years and an executive head of 2 special schools for 3 years.
April Newton – Vice Chair
Hello, my name is April Newton and I am a co-opted Governor at St George’s. I was appointed in the summer of 2021 and was previously a governor at a local primary school.
I have been a qualified Solicitor since 1997 and am currently an Associate Solicitor at Glanvilles Damant.
I am enjoying getting to know St George’s – the staff, and especially the students. I look forward to contributing to the continued success of the school and getting to know it better.
Hello! My name is Maria and I am a governor at St George’s.
I enjoy my current role as an English lecturer at the Isle of Wight College teaching GCSE, Functional Skills and ESOL programmes.
In my spare time, I enjoy spending time with my family and friends and exploring the island.
I believe in giving everyone the best chance and appropriate support. I am keen to give back to the community by building links between different stages of education.
I look forward to contributing to the high levels of standards of support and care, and educational provision of the school.
Karen Cassford – Staff Governor
I have been at St Georges school since 2017 and over the years have progressed from an LSA to currently holding an instructor position supporting pupils with PMLD and SLD. During this time, I have developed a strong understanding of inclusive practice, safeguarding and personalised learning. I have previously been Chair of Governors at a local primary school where I developed confidence in analysing information, asking questions and providing constructive challenge to help ensure the best outcomes for pupils.
Having lived and travelled in countries including India, Australia and Japan, I bring a broad understanding of diversity, inclusion and different perspectives. As a parent of two children in secondary education, I also offer a valuable parental perspective on wellbeing, curriculum and transition.
I hope to continue progressing in my career and aspire to become a qualified teacher in the future.
I am a Class Teacher at St George’s School and have been part of the school community for the past two years. Prior to joining St George’s, I worked in two SEND schools and three mainstream primary schools, gaining experience as both a Teaching Assistant and a Teacher. This varied background has provided me with a broad understanding of the diverse needs of pupils and the importance of inclusive education.
I became a Staff Governor because I wanted to develop my understanding of how decisions are made within a school and the wider impact these decisions have across the whole school community. I recognise the important role of a Staff Governor as a link between school staff and decision-makers, and I am committed to proactively sharing the lived experiences of the classroom to help inform the school’s strategic direction.
My particular area of interest is communication and ensuring that it is delivered in ways that meet the needs of all learners. I am passionate about supporting approaches that enable every pupil to access learning and achieve their full potential.
Outside of school, I enjoy horse riding, which provides me with opportunities to challenge myself, develop resilience, and spend time outdoors.
It is essential that governing bodies recruit and develop governors with the skills to deliver their core functions effectively. However, it is equally important to emphasise that the skills required are those to oversee the success of the school, not to do the school’s job for it. For example, a governor with financial expertise should use their skills to scrutinise the school’s accounts, not to help prepare them. If a governor does possess skills that the school wishes to utilise on a pro bono basis, then it is important that this is considered voluntary work and not governance, and steps should be taken to ensure that this does not blur lines of accountability.
St George’s School Governing Body is set up in the following way:
Parent Governors are elected by other parents at the school
The Staff Governor is elected by all the school staff
The Headteacher is a member of the Governing Body by virtue of their office
The Local Authority Governor is nominated by the Local Authority but appointed by the Governing Body
Co-opted Governors are appointed by the Governing Body
Instrument of Government (constitution) for St George’s School sets out the following:
1 Local Authority Governor
1 Headteacher Governor
9 Co-opted Governors

Welcome to St George’s School
Our Commitment to Every Child
In the community of St George’s School everyone is considered as an individual and is valued equally. Everyone is made to feel welcome and has a voice.
Our school is a safe place to achieve, have fun and to develop skills towards individual, informed paths as we leave school and move forward in life towards adulthood. We learn to make choices for now and the future and to become as independent and self-sufficient as possible taking our place in society as part of Modern Britain. We do our personal best and celebrate our achievements however large or small. As a team we experience the world and work towards achieving our goals and dreams and being the best we can be.
The Governing Body and Staff team at St. George’s School are fully committed to and embody the following:
St George’s School works towards fulfilling aspirations and celebrating personal achievements. We learn to make choices which shape our future enabling us to have our voices heard, be respected, develop resilience and independence to take our place in society.

Curriculum Pathways
It is our aim that all students, regardless of background, ethnicity, or level of need, are supported to achieve their full potential through access to quality first-class teaching and appropriately differentiated learning activities and approaches.
Our long-term goal is to help equip our students with the knowledge and skills they need to live fulfilling and independent lives, achieving the goals and aspirations that our students set for themselves, with the support of all those around them.

Key Stage 3
Information
It is our aim within Key Stage 3 that all students, regardless of background, ethnicity, or level of need, are supported to achieve their full potential through access to quality first-class teaching and appropriately differentiated learning activities and approaches.
Our long-term goal is to help equip our students with the knowledge and skills they need to live fulfilling and independent lives, achieving the goals and aspirations that our students set for themselves, with the support of all those around them.
Intent
The Key Stage 3 curriculum has been designed to create a balance between formal/semi-formal classroom learning and a range of experiences across the school and which allows students the opportunities to broaden their life experiences.
Our curriculum provides students with experiences and opportunities which best meet their learning and developmental needs. Through clear strategic planning, our curriculum provides opportunities from which the students can learn and develop transferrable skills building a foundation on which they can progress into accreditation in key stage 4 and 5.
The acquisition of knowledge and the development of skills is carefully planned to create a purposeful and exciting learning journey for every young person.
In order to ensure that progression and balance are maintained, teachers plan and tailor units of work and lessons to address the specific individual needs of students so that all students are able to reach their full potential regardless of their starting point.

Key Stage 4
Intent
The KS4 curriculum is designed to build upon the knowledge and developing skills gained in KS3, with a clear sense of purpose and direction for each individual learner. Our approach is centred on what students need to learn next, ensuring that planning is responsive to each student’s strengths, needs, and aspirations.
We aim to equip students with the essential academic, personal, and technical skills required to prepare them for their next stage of education or training.
A key focus is developing students’ independence and confidence, enabling them to apply their learning in real-life contexts across a range of settings.
We promote the development of safe, responsible citizens who are able to advocate for themselves with confidence and respect.
We also aim to broaden students’ horizons by providing opportunities to explore future pathways through workshops, visiting speakers, meaningful encounters with employers, and workplace visits.
Implementation
The KS4 curriculum is structured around the development of functional and core skills, supporting students from Pre-Entry to Level 2. It is designed to equip learners with the practical knowledge and skills needed to live independently, continue learning, and engage successfully in adulthood and the world of work.
During Key Stage 4, students work towards a range of accreditations, typically delivered through one- or two-year courses depending on subject pathways. Accredited subjects include English, Maths, ICT, Religion and Worldviews, Science, Art, Physical Education, Food Technology, and Independent Living.
Assessment is ongoing and varied, including teacher assessment, internally completed coursework, and externally set or moderated assessments where appropriate.

These skills are embedded across the curriculum to develop resilience, perseverance, and self-belief.
In addition, students are provided with opportunities to engage in work-related learning, community activities, and real-life experiences that reinforce classroom learning.

Impact
St George’s Key Stage 4 Curriculum Design
Students in Key Stage 4 are grouped into mixed year class groups based on academic level and on social needs. Students follow a Life Skills Pathway or a Vocational Pathway depending on their Pathway to Adulthood.
Students on a Vocational Pathway are working towards employment and living independently.
Students on a Life Skills Pathway are building steps to more independence, autonomy and self-advocacy within a supported adult life.
Students can move between Pathways depending on their individual choices, progress and needs.
As with Key Stage 3, classes follow a model of having one teacher with a pastoral role, who will teach the majority of core lessons, undertake day to day contact with families, compile EHCP annual reviews and be the main contact for parents and carers.
Maths and English
Students begin their Functional Skills curriculum.
For English and Maths, students work towards gaining accreditations in Pre Entry, Entry 1, Entry 2, Entry 3, and then Level 1. Some students will be learning practically and compiling a portfolio of evidence for assessment and others will sit formal exams.
Core lessons
Class based lessons are Life Skills, Work Skills, RSHE, Religion and World view.
These are designed to be differentiated for learners accessing the different pathways and Lazer qualifications can be achieved.
Accredited Specialist subjects
Students will transition to specialist teachers for Art, Physical Education and Science and Food Technology twice per week per subject These lessons are taught by teachers with a subject specialism in their own specialist classroom or area such as the gym or field for PE. The class team of teaching assistants will also transition to specialists with the students. Specialist teachers may make contact with families if required regarding their subjects.

Key Stage 5
Sixth Form Information
Intent
St George’s Sixth Form aims to deliver a varied curriculum centred on the skills, knowledge and experiences needed for each individual’s pathway to adulthood, and to provide our learners with the best holistic education to prepare them for their next steps. Our curriculum considers the needs and aspirations of individual learners and their different pathways, and is ambitious in providing them with the tools to become successful adults and undertake their individual next steps confidently and effectively with the greatest amount of autonomy and independence.
Implementation
The curriculum is designed around the learning of functional, core skills to equip students from Pre Entry through to Level 2 with the practical skills they need to live, learn, and work, or engage in adulthood successfully.
The curriculum is designed around a combination of Maths and English, based round Functional Skills programmes, at a level appropriate to the student, through a range of delivery routes, from formal lessons to practical Life Skills based activities. Students can complete formal assessment, or Quality Mark Accreditation from Pre Entry – L2.
The curriculum also includes Life Skills, Work Skills, RSHE, RaW, Volunteer Work, accessing the community, work placements and Supported Internships. These provide students with practical skills and knowledge to prepare them for their own pathways, whether they be, bespoke packages, Further Education or Care Providers, Supported Living, Independent Living or Work.
Vocational Options are a core part of each student’s curriculum, which feed into next steps to local Further Education Providers, Local Employment Sectors, areas of student interest, for personal development, student aspiration and a set of core skills for adulthood.
At the heart of our Sixth Form are our school values: Aspiration, Resilience, Independence and Respect. These underpin our curriculum and the ethos of the Sixth Form. At St George’s Sixth Form, we place great importance on a curriculum, which develops the whole person in preparation for their individual next steps. Through our core values, we foster an environment where development of the; cognition and Learning, communication and interaction, physical and sensory needs, social, emotional and mental health, of each child is considered. We firmly believe that everyone is entitled to an ambitious, curriculum, tailored to suit their style and stage of learning.
Impact
St George’s 6th form Curriculum Design
Students in the 6th form are grouped into mixed year class groups based on academic level and on social needs. Students follow a Life Skills Pathway or a Vocational Pathway depending on their Pathway to Adulthood.
Students on a Vocational Pathway are working towards employment and living independently.
Students on a Life Skills Pathway are building steps to more independence, autonomy and self-advocacy within a supported adult life.
Students can move between Pathways depending on their individual choices, progress and needs.
Students may leave 6th form in either Year 12, Year 13 or Year 14. Course content for class-based lessons roll across 3 years so that students are able to build units from year 12-14 in mixed year cohorts.
Maths and English
Students begin their Functional Skills curriculum based on their Year 11 attainment levels.
For English and Maths, students leave their class groups and go into streamed classes. These are streamed at the following levels: Pre Entry, Entry 1, Entry 2, Entry 3, Level 1. Some students will be learning practically and compiling a portfolio of evidence for assessment and others will sit formal exams.
Core lessons
Class based lessons are Life Skills, RSHE, Religion and World view. Students on Vocational Pathways also complete an accreditation in Work Skills.
These are designed to be differentiated for learners accessing the different pathways.
Accredited Options
Students can choose 2 Options to study as part of their individual programme of study. These run on Tuesday and Wednesday afternoons. Where possible teachers link with local businesses and organisations to ensure students have real life experience with the world of work in their chosen Options, as well as planning in both practical and Enterprising activities into their school based offer.
These are reviewed yearly based on both student aspiration and labour market information specific to the Isle of Wight market.
